story: LensFleet began with a simple observation: a status update is not proof. "Delivered", "visited", "patrolled", "on site" are claims, and every dispute, insurance claim and complaint starts with a claim nobody can check. LensFleet puts a lens on the movement — a dashcam on the bus, a body camera on the guard or carer, a tracker on the generator or the dog — and turns the claim into something that can be seen, placed on a map, timestamped and shared.

We started with goods in transit. The same need turned out to exist everywhere people and things move: a security firm that has to answer for an incident, a care agency whose client's daughter wants to know the carer came, a vlogger who wants viewers to ride along live, a plant-hire company that keeps losing track of generators. The platform did not change; the sectors multiplied. Today LensFleet serves six of them and is built so that the seventh needs no new code — only new words in the interface.
mission: To give any organisation or household a camera-enabled, location-aware platform that records what happened, where and when, protects that record, and lets it be shared with exactly the people who need to see it — no more, no less.
vision: A world in which the movement of people, goods and services is transparent, trusted and verifiable, so that the people who depend on it can act on evidence rather than assumption.
